items.stemHtml: A 61-year-old woman had a parathyroid adenoma removed 3 days ago after years of primary hyperparathyroidism with osteitis fibrosa cystica (preoperative calcium 13.1 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 640 U/L). She now has perioral tingling and carpopedal spasm. Serum calcium is 6.9 mg/dL, phosphorus 1.8 mg/dL, magnesium 1.2 mEq/L and alkaline phosphatase 590 U/L. Intact PTH is 70 pg/mL (N = 10–65). Which of the following best explains her hypocalcemia?

options.label: A
options.html: Accidental removal of all four parathyroid glands

options.label: B
options.html: Calcium-sensing receptor activation by low magnesium

options.label: C
options.html: Increased renal calcium loss from postoperative volume expansion

options.label: D
options.html: Rapid uptake of calcium and phosphate into demineralised bone

options.label: E
options.html: Resistance of the kidney to parathyroid hormone

items.explanationHtml:
This is hungry bone syndrome. After long-standing, high-turnover hyperparathyroid bone disease (high alkaline phosphatase, osteitis fibrosa cystica), removing the PTH stimulus lets osteoblast activity continue while resorption stops, so bone rapidly takes up calcium, phosphate and magnesium. The clue that separates it from postoperative hypoparathyroidism is the low phosphate with a PTH that is not low; in hypoparathyroidism phosphate rises. Treatment is large doses of calcium, often with calcitriol and magnesium.

Takeaway: hypocalcemia after parathyroidectomy with LOW phosphate and non-suppressed PTH is hungry bone syndrome; high phosphate suggests hypoparathyroidism.

whyNot.A: Loss of all parathyroid tissue would give a low PTH and a high phosphate.
whyNot.B: Low magnesium impairs PTH secretion and action, but here PTH is not low, and magnesium is falling for the same reason calcium is: uptake into bone.
whyNot.C: Volume expansion causes only small changes and would not lower phosphate and magnesium this much.
whyNot.E: PTH resistance (pseudohypoparathyroidism) gives a high phosphate and a very high PTH, and it is congenital.

items.objective: Distinguish hungry bone syndrome from hypoparathyroidism after parathyroidectomy.
